The PanoRef multi-origin optimizer implementation is now a real algorithm (not just occlusion foundation), adding 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs rather than greedily selecting the best first origin. The surface sampler is deterministic and correctly samples triangles in proportion to world-space area using barycentric coordinates. Origin evaluation includes actual segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility and usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values. The shared coarse-to-fine engine uses 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, and separate fixed-first and joint branches. Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes.

However, the reviewer rates algorithm architecture 8/10, correctness of search modes 7.5/10, and readiness for complex imported sets 4/10—overall promising but not production-ready. Six blockers are identified: (1) Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because obstacle clearance uses per-object AABBs rather than actual geometry, causing points inside large imported objects to be rejected; fix requires actual geometry clearance via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance or shapecast, with per-connected-mesh or spatial-cluster obstacle bounds. (2) Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports—every triangle is expanded to JavaScript objects with three Vec3 arrays, normals, IDs, and area; 3 million triangles require ~144 MB minimum packed data but actual representation is several times larger, plus structured-cloning into the worker and BVH sorting of JS index arrays, with millions of temporary three-element array allocations causing GC pressure; fix requires compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions, Uint32Array indices, optional Float32Array normals, Uint32Array meshRanges, Float32Array transforms), transferable ArrayBuffers, and either three-mesh-bvh, a flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries, avoiding expansion of indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle. (3) Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because extractCoverageScene is called synchronously before creating/posting to the worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning freeze the app before the worker reports progress; fix requires moving extraction into the worker or chunking it with yields between meshes. (4) 'Apply to selected panorama pair' is conceptually wrong—the UI allows optimized origins to be written directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference, but changing metadata does not transform the image from the new position, merely projecting old pixels from the wrong point and ruining alignment; correct workflow preserves existing panoramas, moves capture origins, renders new graybox panoramas, inpaints/generates styled panoramas, imports them as new panoramas, and associates each with its actual origin—never rewriting origins of already captured panoramas. (5) The reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent because reachableCoverage uses the coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates while final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed + 1, allowing the UI to show Combined coverage 83%, Reachable upper bound 80%, Reachable captured 100%; additionally, fixed-first mode calculates the reachable set before evaluating the arbitrary first origin, so the fixed first origin is not included in the reachable upper bound at all; fix requires a common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, and including the fixed origin in the reachable union for fixed-first mode. (6) Fixed-first mode does not enforce minimum separation—joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation, but fixed-first mode's rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position or distance, so even an identical candidate position can survive; fix requires distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.

Important refinements: The 'four-level refinement' is not truly iterative—offsets are generated around the original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ± spacing/4, ± spacing/8, ± spacing/16) without selecting the best half-step result and centering the quarter-step search around that new result; it is a useful multiresolution neighborhood sample but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in the plan. Local candidates can float between floors because candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below the candidate, and local offsets retain the original Y coordinate; on sloped terrain or multilevel sets, an offset can move over a lower floor while preserving the upper floor's camera height, leaving the panorama origin floating several meters above the new floor—fix requires for each offset: find the floor under the new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance. The optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules—the optimizer evaluates angle and texel density, but when both panoramas are visible, the actual shader blends them only by distance, so the optimized coverage result and visible result do not fully agree; the shader should use the same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging.

Testing assessment: Current tests are good unit tests but the most dangerous cases are absent: one large imported object containing an entire room, a 100k+ triangle performance fixture, reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped and multilevel floors, existing panorama origins remaining immutable, and candidate generation inside concave imported geometry. There are no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to the latest head, so the reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI.

Recent actions: A stale test guarding the old distance-only blend heuristic was removed; the dead shader constant PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0 was removed; the assertion was replaced with one protecting the new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0 and projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0, projectedQualityAt, no projectedConfidence); the targeted regression test (tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts, 36 tests) passed. Full test suite (42 test files, 371 tests) passed, lint (tsc --noEmit) passed, and build (vite build) passed. The reviewer's directive: rebase onto main and resolve the PR conflict; add an allowed-floor-region mechanism or at least robust imported-floor component filtering; run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely a BVH-construction test; set a goal to accomplish the above, and when work is complete, spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that the goal is actually fully complete, have it report back what still is lacking, then fix that, and repeat until the subagent is unable to find any holes in the implementation.

The PanoRef coverage optimizer added an explicit Allowed floor region mechanism to resolve geometrically ambiguous large horizontal surfaces (large roofs/platforms/prop tops) that connected-component filtering alone cannot exclude. The UI (CoverageOptimizerPanel.tsx) adds a toggle and X/Y/Z min/max numeric inputs defaulting to a 5m box around the capture origin at camera height; when enabled, extractCoverageScene receives the region and the optimizer restricts floor candidates to points inside those bounds. Engine changes: types.ts adds allowedFloorRegions?: CoverageBounds[]; surfaceSampler.ts normalizes regions, stores them on the scene, and when present uses triangle-vs-region intersection instead of connected-component filtering for floor selection; candidateGenerator.ts adds floorPointIsAllowed and gates coarse/fine candidate generation and final position checks. A regression test (tests/projectionCoverage.test.ts) verifies an allowed region rejects a 6×6 imported object's large 0.8–1.5m top while retaining the 0–3m floor and producing candidates at 1.6m. Docs/README were updated to describe the feature and the audit doc was updated to list explicit allowed-floor rejection. A first patch attempt failed apply_patch verification on README, and a subsequent typecheck run failed (TS2322 on Field key prop and CoverageBounds Vec3 typing); these were fixed by removing key from Field and casting normalized region min/max as Vec3. After fixes, targeted tests, lint, and the relevant test files were re-run. The base capsule also notes the broader PR context: 6 remaining blockers, reviewer directive to rebase/resolve conflict and add allowed-floor or robust imported-floor filtering plus a 100k+ benchmark, and a first audit that disproved completion on unpublished rebased history and a disconnected 3×3 tabletop; the allowed-floor-region fix is the substantive response to the tabletop/ambiguous-top issue, with publication deferred until a fresh auditor finds no holes.

Round two adversarial audit found one concrete hole: allowed-floor controls remained editable during a running analysis, so edits did not cancel or invalidate the in-flight job and a stale result could appear under newly displayed or invalid bounds. The fix disabled the floor-region toggle and all six X/Y/Z min/max fields while status === 'running', with a browser regression asserting controls lock and unlock around the optimizer job. The change was applied via Field.tsx Toggle disabled support and CoverageOptimizerPanel.tsx gating, committed as 'Lock coverage floor bounds during analysis' (4153429), pushed to t3code/projector-occlusion, and verified by lint, typecheck, unit tests (uiFidelity 40 tests, projectionCoverage 11 tests including the 100k+ integration), production build, and e2e coverage-optimizer tests on desktop and phone. PR #23 remained MERGEABLE after the push, and adversarial audit round three was started against commit 4153429.

Round three adversarial audit identified two stale-state holes: editing bounds after a completed run left old results and origin-apply actions visible even when origins were outside the newly displayed region, and changing the primary panorama did not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result, leaving the region centered on the previous panorama. The in-flight locking fix from round two remained sound. The fix centralized result invalidation for every optimizer input and synchronized only untouched default bounds to the active capture origin while preserving user-authored bounds. Implementation added a defaultFloorRegion helper, a floorRegionTouchedRef, a captureInputKey derived from primaryPano id/origin/dimensions/cameraHeight, a previousCaptureInputKeyRef, and an invalidateAnalysis function that increments analysisIdRef, cancels the task, clears taskRef, and resets status/result/message. The mode Select, restrictFloorRegion Toggle, and floor min/max TextInputs now call invalidateAnalysis on change, with floor inputs also setting floorRegionTouchedRef.current = true. A useEffect watches cameraHeight, captureInputKey, and captureOrigin; when the key changes it invalidates the analysis and, if the floor region has not been touched, resets floorRegion to defaultFloorRegion(captureOrigin, cameraHeight). The patch was applied to src/components/common/CoverageOptimizerPanel.tsx and e2e/layout-and-workflow.spec.ts (adding a floor-min edit assertion that expects zero results and zero apply-capture buttons). Verification passed lint (tsc --noEmit), unit tests (uiFidelity 40 tests, multiOriginInteraction 36 tests, projectionCoverage 11 tests including the 100k+ triangle integration at 35.8s), production build (vite, 8.31s, with a chunk-size warning), and e2e coverage-optimizer tests on desktop-chromium (1.0m) and phone-390 (34.5s). The commit 'Invalidate stale coverage optimizer results' (4f4fd39) was pushed to t3code/projector-occlusion, updating 4153429..4f4fd39 across 2 files with 72 insertions and 27 deletions; PR #23 remained MERGEABLE with mergeStateStatus CLEAN (headRefOid 41534294b0f5b67b82317c50a7060352576675c5). Audit round four was started afterward.

Round four adversarial audit found one remaining cancellation hole: stale extraction failures bypass the analysis-identity check and can overwrite a newer analysis state with `failed`. The fix adds the same identity guard to the extraction catch and a regression guard around that cancellation boundary. PR #23 remains MERGEABLE/CLEAN with local and remote heads matching current origin/main. Verified invariants include bounds and capture-input changes invalidating successful results, region enforcement covering worker/candidate/refinement paths, heavy two-mode integration and real benchmark evidence, and recorded typecheck/build/WebGL/browser/workflow verification. A uiFidelity test was added to assert four analysis-identity guards and the extraction catch guard; initial run showed only two matches and failed, then the patch was applied and re-verified with lint and uiFidelity tests.

Audit round five found no remaining concrete holes. The stale extraction-failure path now checks analysis identity before mutating status, with a regression protecting both the success and failure guards; the fix was committed and pushed as 80882e3 on t3code/projector-occlusion, rebased on current origin/main, with PR #23 showing MERGEABLE/CLEAN and passing Netlify deploy-preview checks. A uiFidelity test was added to assert the four analysis-identity guards plus the extraction catch guard; after the patch it passed alongside lint and the full test suite. Final clean-head verification ran 373/373 tests (including real WebGL pixel readback and the 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer) and a 33.1 MB workflow export smoke, after which a documentation-only stale count in docs/ui-revamp-regression-audit.md was corrected from 303/303 to 373/373. The auditor confirmed no new gap from the final mechanical commit.

Final adversarial audit round six found no concrete holes on published HEAD c1f6c8d. PR #23 is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with all Netlify deploy-preview checks complete (header/redirect/pages rules NEUTRAL, deploy-preview SUCCESS). The branch t3code/projector-occlusion is synchronized locally and remotely, rebased on current origin/main (merge-base 3a9017438ef6ecccd4d029bc8b10f9eec4352c66), and the temporary local vite preview process (PID 33292) was stopped after browser verification. A documentation-only commit c1f6c8d corrected the coverage verification count in docs/ui-revamp-regression-audit.md from 303/303 to 373/373 (1 file, 1 insertion, 1 deletion), introducing no runtime or configuration change. The prior base capsule confirms audit round five also found no remaining concrete holes, with the stale extraction-failure path guarded by analysis identity checks (commit 80882e3, PR #23 MERGEABLE/CLEAN, Netlify checks passing, uiFidelity test added for four analysis-identity guards plus extraction catch guard, 373/373 tests passing including real WebGL pixel readback and 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer, 33.1 MB workflow export smoke). Goal status set to complete: objective satisfied across six adversarial audit rounds (four found and fixed actionable gaps; rounds five and six found no holes), 688,000 tokens used over ~1 hour 4 minutes. No new gap introduced by the final mechanical documentation commit; auditor confirmed clean state.
